chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

'Indeed, for every innovation (bid'a) that occurs after me, by which faith (iman) is intended to be undermined, there is a guardian from the people of my household appointed for it — he defends (faith) against it, speaking by inspiration from God, declaring the Truth and illuminating it, and repelling the plots of the schemers, speaking on behalf of the weak ones. Therefore take heed, O people of insight, and rely upon God.'

key_terms.أُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ: uli al-absar — 'people of insight/vision', a Quranic phrase (59:2) calling people to draw lessons from what they observe
key_terms.الْإِيمَانُ: iman — faith or belief, particularly the core doctrinal commitment of a Muslim, distinct from mere outward practice
key_terms.بِإِلْهَامٍ: ilham — divine inspiration or inner revelation, distinct from wahy (prophetic revelation) but similarly granted by God to guide the Imam
key_terms.بِدْعَةٍ: bid'a — religious innovation introduced without scriptural basis, viewed in classical Islamic jurisprudence as potentially corrupting to sound doctrine and practice
key_terms.مُوَكَّلًا: muwakkal — appointed, commissioned, or entrusted (by God) with a specific protective role
key_terms.وَلِيّاً: wali — guardian, protector, or appointed authority; in Shia theology, this specifically refers to the divinely-ordained Imam from the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about guardians from the Ahlulbayt protecting faith from innovations?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) as guaranteeing that for every religious innovation that threatens faith, Allah appoints a guardian from the Ahl al-Bayt (AS) to defend against it through divine inspiration. The statement was transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to reassure believers during a period of intense theological disputation, when various movements — from the Murji'a to the Mu'tazila — were introducing doctrines that Shia scholars held to be deviations. The phrase 'people of insight' (uli al-absar) invokes a Quranic call to reflection, urging the community to recognize these divinely-guided guardians and place their full trust in God.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Maboub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘

After mesaw innovations will be fabricated in order to destroy the Eman, however, a Guardianasws from the Peopleasws of mysaww Household would come forward to remove it (the innovations). Heasws would speak with the inspiration from Allahazwj, and heasws would declare the Truth and radiate it, and heasws would repeal the plots of the plotters, speaking on behalf of the weak ones. Therefore take a lesson, O people of insight, and rely upon Allahazwj!’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Mu‘awiya ibn Wahab who has said the following. “Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said that the holy Prophet has said, ‘

It is certain that against every innovation with plots to destroy faith there will be an (religious) authority from my family as guardian of faith and as its defender. (Such) authority will speak on inspiration from Allah to declare the truth and bring it to light, repulse and foil the evil plots of the agents of wickedness and speak for the weak. O people of Intelligence, take a lesson from it and trust Allah.’”
